text:
Marco Rossi came to Vancouver as a center who'd shown he could produce, and the first months haven't delivered. Seven points in 17 games, no goals in his last ten, and a shooting percentage (9.7%) below where he should settle. Manny Malhotra has been asked publicly to explain the lack of production, per The Hockey News, which tells you where the conversation in Vancouver has gone.

Some context helps. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.6 wins last season, 79th among forwards, mostly from the power play, with teammates in the bottom 8% by impact. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows 70% of his zone exits leave with possession, one of the cleaner breakout records among forwards. The tools are still there.

The Canucks have taken 40% of the expected goals with him on the ice, which is roughly the team's level, not worse. Since Filip Chytil's injury his minutes have ticked back up. Our range has him at 31 to 52 points over a full season, and the goals should come: he gets chances, just not finishes. Daniel Wagner liked a recent smart pass as "a good start." It needs to become a run.
headline: Rossi needs a run
